channel.title: The Retreat Register — Updates
channel.description: Verification progress from The Retreat Register, published with real numbers: coverage snapshots, data findings, and what gets cut from the register and why.

item.title: How to Plan a Church Retreat: Protect Minors and Volunteers First
item.description: Plan a church retreat around the people it must protect: a coordinator, permission forms for minors and the venue's insurance in writing.

item.title: Family Retreat Ideas: Plan a Multi-Generation Weekend Under One Roof
item.description: Plan a family retreat where every age fits: a place that sleeps everyone, a kitchen to share and quiet rooms for rest.

item.title: Retreat Themes for Work: Pick One the Agenda Can Carry
item.description: Pick a work retreat theme that names the goal, then let it shape the sessions, the venue and the invite.

item.title: Retreat Food Menu: Plan Group Meals Around the Sessions
item.description: Plan retreat meals around the agenda: lighter food before working sessions, one long dinner, and dietary needs counted first.

item.title: How to Plan a Women's Retreat: A Checklist From Venue to Last Night
item.description: A women's retreat checklist that works for a church group or a group of friends, from the venue to the last night.

item.title: Corporate Retreat, the 2026 Film: How Real Retreat Planning Differs
item.description: The film Corporate Retreat set beside how a real company retreat is planned, from the goal to the venue contract.

item.title: Yoga Retreat Insurance: Hosts Check Whether Teacher Cover Travels
item.description: Whether a yoga teacher's own policy covers teaching at a retreat, and the questions a host puts to the insurer in writing.

item.title: Family Reunion Organizers: Choose a Lodge, Cabins or a Group Camp
item.description: Choose where a large family reunion sleeps: one lodge, a cluster of cabins or a group camp, and the bed and bathroom questions to ask first.

item.title: Strategic Planning Retreat Agenda: Sessions That End in Decisions
item.description: A strategic planning retreat agenda where every session answers one question and the day ends with decisions that have owners.

item.title: Youth Retreat Ideas: Plan the Program and the Supervision Together
item.description: Youth retreat ideas planned beside their supervision: who watches each activity, where it happens, and what the permission form covers.

item.title: Retreat Venue Contract: The Clauses Planners Read Before Signing
item.description: The sections of a retreat venue contract to read before the price: rooms, meeting space, food minimums, deposits and cancellation.

item.title: Offsite Meaning for Organizers: What a Company Offsite Covers
item.description: What a company offsite is, how it differs from a meeting at the office, and whether to write offsite or off-site.

item.title: Hotel Attrition Allowance: How Planners Read It Before Signing
item.description: What the attrition allowance in a room block contract means, and how to tell whether it counts per night or over the whole stay.

item.title: How to Plan a Board Retreat: Set the Objectives, Then Pick the Room
item.description: Plan a board retreat from its objectives: agree them with the chair and the chief executive, then choose the agenda and the room.

item.title: Leadership Retreat Topics: Choose the Few the Team Must Decide
item.description: How to pick leadership retreat topics the team must decide together, and keep the list shorter than the days allow.

item.title: Team Retreat Agenda: Build a Two-Day Schedule With Free Time
item.description: A two-day team retreat agenda with focused mornings, free afternoons and one shared evening, plus who runs each block.

item.title: Hiring a DJ for a Company Offsite: What Planners Ask the Venue
item.description: Before booking a DJ, planners ask the venue about noise curfews, outside vendors and the insurance a vendor must show.

item.title: Retreat Center Insurance: What Owners Carry Before Hosting Groups
item.description: The cover a retreat center holds before groups arrive, and the proof of insurance owners ask each renting group to send.

item.title: Retreat ROI: Build the One-Page Report Planners Send to Leadership
item.description: Show leadership what a retreat achieved. Pick one or two outcomes before the trip, log each decision and its owner, and send a one-page report within two weeks.

item.title: Team Retreat Activities: Choose by Goal and Check the Venue Can Host Them
item.description: An activity earns its place on the agenda when it serves the retreat's goal. How to pick by purpose, and the venue questions each kind of activity raises.
